Michael Tatum]] |jpva=[[Kazuya Nakai]] }} |} '''Brassius''' (Japanese: '''コルサ''' ''Colsa''[https://static.mercdn.net/item/detail/orig/photos/m86751994252_1.jpg "Colsa & Usokkie" POKÉMON TRAINERS collectible card from Pikachu Sweets by Pokémon Cafe]) is an artist who is the [[Gym Leader]] of [[Artazon]]'s [[Gym]], known officially as the [[Artazon Gym]]. He [[Type expert|specializes]] in {{type|Grass}} {{OBP|Pokémon|species}}. He hands out the {{badge|PaldeaGrass|Grass Badge}} to {{pkmn|Trainer}}s who defeat him. ==In the core series games== Brassius is one of the Gym Leaders of the [[Paldea]] region, and is also an artist. He treats battles as an artform and tests the aesthetic sensibilities of those who challenge his Gym. He is always busy with a new project when he's not battling, inspired by his surroundings. In addition to the Gym Badge, Brassius gives out {{TM|020|Trailblaze}} after defeating him. He is close friends with [[Hassel]], the art teacher at the academy in [[Mesagoza]]. Hassel helped inspire Brassius's most remarkable artwork called "Surrendering Sunflora", a statue installation spread around the town of Artazon depicting {{p|Sunflora}} with somber expressions. Amongst art connoisseurs, the meaning of "Surrendering Sunflora" is debated.(September 7, 2022). "[https://scarletviolet.pokemon.com/en-us/news/treasure_hunt/ Your Own Story, Woven Through Your Treasure Hunt]." Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet Official Website In truth, at the time of the creation of "Surrendering Sunflora", Brassius was deathly ill, and he had given up all hope, even prepared to give up being an artist if "Surrendering Sunflora" didn't gain proper recognition. Despite feeling his worst, Hassel was there to encourage him, which gave Brassius the strength to start the project in the first place. Whether this event took place while he was a Gym Leader is unknown. Another installment around Artazon by Brassius is "The Harvest", a collective of flower-like sculptures ranging in color, each with six bulbs equidistance around a ring, possibly inspired by {{p|Arboliva}}. In [[The Indigo Disk]], Brassius can be invited to act as a special coach at [[Blueberry Academy]]. ===Challenging the Artazon Gym=== Artazon Gym Leader: Brassius (AKA the Verdant Virtuoso) "This Grass-type user and artist is a first stop for many fledgling Trainers. His Sudowoodo is capable of Sync {{Tera}}stallizing into the {{t|Grass}} type. Brassius became a playable sync pair on January 16, 2026. {{PairDex/h|Grass}} {{PairDex|243|Brassius|trainerlink=Brassius (Masters)#Sudowoodo|trainerimg=Brassius|0185 Tera Grass|Sudowoodo|buddy=yes|gender=male|tera=Grass|Grass|Flying|Tech|exrole=Sprint|6|EX Fair Sync Pair Scout}} |} ==Quotes== {{main|Brassius/Quotes}} ==In animation== [[File:Brassius anime.png|thumb|250px|Brassius in {{aniseries|HZ}}]] ===''Pokémon Horizons: The Series''=== Brassius was first mentioned in ''[[HZ009|Welcome to Paldea!]]'', with [[Alex]] mentioning that he has seen a rare Pokémon, which [[Liko]] theorized could've been the [[Black Rayquaza]]. Brassius debuted in ''[[HZ010|Nemona and Brassius and…]]'', where he was revealed to suffer from artist's block and no longer could see any quality in any of his works. Liko, [[Roy]], and [[Nemona]] stopped by his house for information. Brassius immediately took a liking to Liko upon hearing that she is Alex's daughter, inviting her and her friends to his home. Upon being enraged by Roy's question about Rayquaza, he ended the conversation. Later on, after seeing Liko, Roy, and Nemona's motivation to cheer him up by gathering together dozens of {{p|Sunflora}}, Brassius decided to show them his Rayquaza sculpture, explaining that his encounter with Rayquaza had caused his slump. Seeing Roy's animation, Brassius decided to challenge Roy to a battle. With renewed spirit, Brassius managed to win the battle. Before the group left, Brassius decided to show them one more sculpture, this time of a {{pkmn2|giant}} {{p|Arboliva}} that he saw in the forest where Rayquaza appeared. [[File:Roy and Brassius.png|left|thumb|220px|Brassius and Roy]] In ''[[HZ015|Someone We Can't See! Whosawhatsit?]]'', while the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]] were searching for Liko, Brassius was mentioned by Roy as one of the people he visited to find out where she might have gone. Brassius appeared in a flashback to Liko and Roy's journey in ''[[HZ045|From So Far Away]]''. In ''[[HZ046|Welcome to Naranja Academy!]]'', Brassius was selected as Roy's challenge as part of Tera Training. Liko, Roy, and [[Dot]] arrived in Artazon in ''[[HZ048|Sparkle! The Glow of Flame and Art]]'' in order for Roy to challenge him, but Brassius was busy finishing an sculpture to be featured in the [[Artazon Art Festival]]. After seeing Roy's way of battling and his reaction after losing to Nemona, however, he put the test on indefinite hold, declaring Roy can never master {{Tera}}stallization until he finds out what he's missing. Roy followed his advice and, working with his {{TP|Roy|Fuecoco}}, made a sculpture for the festival that showed to Brassius that he had figured it out. Then, they proceeded to the battle court, where the test was held, and Roy managed to win after Terastallizing Fuecoco. In ''[[HZ055|Showdown! The Paldea Elite Four]]'', Brassius attended the [[Naranja Academy]] as was partnered with Roy as part of the [[Elite Four Tag Battle]]. They battled [[Hassel]], using Fuecoco and Dolliv against {{p|Baxcalibur}} and {{p|Flapple}}, only to eventually lose the match. In ''[[HZ067|Shine on, Terastallization! Liko vs. Roy!]]'', Brassius and Hassel watched Roy's battle against Liko, Brassius praised Roy for his improved battling skills and was pleased when he won the match. {{-}} ====Character==== Brassius is a passionate artist who uses Pokémon as his inspiration for his artwork. He uses the word "avant-garde" when something intrigues or upsets him. As a [[Gym Leader]], he uses battling as a way to teach {{pkmn|Trainer}}s and improve their battling skills. ====Pokémon==== =====On hand===== {{TrainerPoké |trainer=Brassius |pkmn=Dolliv |type1=Grass |type2=Normal |img=Brassius Dolliv.png |epnum=HZ010 |epname=Nemona and Brassius and… |vajp=Arisa Shida |vaen=Alejandra Reynoso |desc={{p|Dolliv}} is Brassius's first known Pokémon. It is often seen with him and has a habit of spraying out olive oil when surprised or happy. It reappeared in ''[[HZ048|Sparkle! The Glow of Flame and Art]]''. In ''[[HZ055|Showdown! The Paldea Elite Four]]'', Brassius used Dolliv in his match against [[Hassel]], where it teamed up with [[Roy's Fuecoco]] to battle {{p|Baxcalibur}} and {{p|Flapple}}, only to be defeated. During the [[Elite Four Tag Battle]], Dolliv proved to be an extremely powerful and versatile Pokémon in battle, serving as support for Fuecoco while battling on equal terms even with the type disadvantage against fully evolved Pokémon. Dolliv's known moves are {{m|Seed Bomb}}, {{m|Helping Hand}}, {{m|Grass Knot}}, and {{m|Energy Ball}}.}} {{TrainerPoké |trainer=Brassius |pkmn=Sudowoodo |tera=Grass |type1=Rock |img=Brassius Sudowoodo.png |cap=Brassius's Sudowoodo |img2=Brassius Sudowoodo Terastal.png |cap2=Brassius's Terastallized Sudowoodo |epnum=HZ010 |epname=Nemona and Brassius and… |vajp=Tatsuki Kobe |vaen=Bill Rogers |desc={{p|Sudowoodo}} is Brassius's second known Pokémon. It is capable of {{Tera}}stallizing into a {{t|Grass}} type. Brassius used it in his battle against [[Roy]] and his {{TP|Roy|Fuecoco}}. Despite Fuecoco learning {{m|Stomping Tantrum}} during the battle, Sudowoodo was still able to defeat it after Terastallizing. In ''[[HZ048|Sparkle! The Glow of Flame and Art]]'', Sudowoodo was used to battle Roy and his Fuecoco a second time for his [[Tera Training]] test, only to be defeated. Sudowoodo's known moves are {{m|Rock Throw}}, {{m|Substitute}}, {{m|Taunt}}, {{m|Trailblaze}}, and {{m|Stone Edge}}.}} =====Traveling with===== {| width="50%" | {{ActivePoké|||nick=Rotom Phone|Brassius Rotom Phone.png|size=250px|electric|ghost|link=Rotom Phone}} | | |} ====Works of art==== {| class="roundy" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; background:#{{Grass color dark}}; border:5px solid #{{Grass color}}" |- style="background:#eee;" | class="roundytop" style="overflow:hidden;" | [[File:Artazon Festival entrance.png|x120px]] | class="roundytop" style="overflow:hidden;" | [[File:Sunflora at dawn.png|x120px]] |- style="background:#{{grass color light}};" | class="roundybottom" | "{{pcolor|Sunflora|000}} in the eyes of the {{color2|000|Black Rayquaza|black dragon}}" | class="roundybottom" | "{{pcolor|Sunflora|000}} at dawn" |- style="background:#{{grass color light}};"' |- style="background:#eee;" |} ====Voice actors==== {{vatable|color={{grass color}}|bordercolor={{grass color dark}} |ja=中井和哉 ''Kazuya Nakai'' |en=[[J. New Ability: Dash!!]]''. He was first seen in [[Artazon]], where he approached {{Scarlet}} after noting she had been staring at the "Surrendering {{p|Sunflora}}" for some time. Despite knowing nothing about art, Scarlet gave her own interpretation on what the "Surrendering Sunflora" was supposed to convey. Moved to tears, Brassius praised Scarlet's critique as correct, becoming even more impressed upon learning that she had been able to do it despite not attending any of [[Hassel]]'s art classes. When {{adv|Nemona}} arrived and called Scarlet by name, Brassius recognized her as the one had heard from [[Katy]] and agreed to tell her about the [[treasures of ruin]] if she, in turn, would collaborate with him. He saw Scarlet's usage of the Gym Challenge as a tool for collecting information for her profession as a treasure hunter as similar to his own past, when he had created art only to earn money and recognition. After Scarlet had passed the Gym Test, Brassius agreed to battle her. The battle, which ended in Brassius's defeat, left the Gym Leader inspired for a new art piece, though he agreed to tell her about the treasures of ruin as promised. Although he had little information to provide, Brassius did inform Scarlet that the treasures of ruin referred to a group of Pokémon. As Scarlet left, Brassius suggested she go meet with Hassel at the academy, as he was the one who gave him the information to begin with. {{-}} ====Pokémon==== {{TrainerPoké |trainer=Brassius |pkmn=Petilil |gender=female |type1=Grass |img=Brassius Petilil Adventures.png |epnum=PASV09 |epname=Challenge! Petilil's only known move is {{m|Sleep Powder}}.}} {{TrainerPoké |trainer=Brassius |pkmn=Smoliv |type1=Grass |type2=Normal |img=Brassius Smoliv Adventures.png |img_size=160px |epnum=PASV09 |epname=Challenge! Key frame |} ==In the TCG== [[File:BrassiusObsidianFlames187.jpg|200px|thumb|Brassius in the TCG]] {{main|Brassius (Obsidian Flames 187)}} '''Brassius''' was introduced as a {{TCG|Supporter card}} in the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]] during the English Scarlet & Violet Series (the Japanese Scarlet & Violet Era). It was first released as a Japanese {{TCG|SV-P Promotional cards|SV-P Promotional card}} before releasing in the English {{TCG|Obsidian Flames}} expansion, with artwork by [[GIDORA]]. It allows players to shuffle their hand into the deck and draw cards equal to the number of cards that were in their hand, plus one. {{-}} ==Trivia== * Brassius's Japanese Gym Leader title is {{tt|ネイチャーアーティスト|Nature Artist}}. * His {{p|Sudowoodo}}'s {{t|Grass}} Tera Type alludes to Sudowoodo's mimicry of actual trees. This is referenced by Brassius himself after {{Tera}}stallizing the Pokémon, calling it "Truleewoodo" (Japanese: '''ウソから出た{{tt|実|まこと}}''' ''truth from lies''). In the English dub of ''[[HZ010|Nemona and Brassius and…]]'', this is retranslated more closely as "From Fiction Comes Truth". * Of the eight [[Gym Leader]]s of [[Paldea]], Brassius is the only one not to be seen holding a {{i|Poké Ball}} prior to calling out his first Pokémon. * After Brassius recalls his Pokémon from battle, he touches the Poké Ball to his forehead rather than simply nodding at it like many other {{pkmn|Trainer}}s. * Brassius was designed by [[Megumi Mizutani]].[https://twitter.com/megtany/status/1984426148626133440 Twitter post about designing Katy, Brassius, Iono, and Tulip] ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{grass color}}; border:3px solid #{{grass color dark}}" |- ! style="background:#{{grass color light}}" | Language ! style="background:#{{grass color light}}" | Name ! style="background:#{{grass color light}}" | Origin |- | Japanese | コルサ ''Colsa'' | From ''colza'' (Spanish for "{{wp|rapeseed}}") |- | English, Italian | Brassius | From ''Brassica napus'' (scientific name of rapeseed) |- | German | Colzo | Similar to his Japanese name |- | European Spanish,
